mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The meaning of سُبْحَانَ الله is declaring Allah free of evil; this is related from the Prophet ﷺ. It is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though it were put in the place of سبحت الله تسبيحا ("I glorified Allah with a glorification"). It is definite when used alone, and at its end are two augments, the alif and the nūn, so it is a diptote because of definiteness and the two augments. It is related from Sībawayh that some of the Arabs make it indefinite and say سبحانًا with nunation. Abū ʿUbayd said it is accusative as a vocative, as though He said "O glory of Allah, O glory of Him who carried by night (يَا سُبْحَانَ الله يَا سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أسرى)".

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His saying {قل لَو أَنْتُم}: "لولا" [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense requires لو — "لو is followed only by a verb"] is followed only by a verb, because it carries the meaning of condition; if [the verb] is not overt, it is implied. So it is implied here, and أنتم is nominative as the agent of the implied verb.

mekki-muskil:101-101.t:
His saying {تسع آيَات بَيِّنَات}: it is permissible for بينات to be in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of آيات, or in the position of accusative as a naʿt of تسع.
His saying {وبالحق أَنزَلْنَاهُ وبالحق نزل}: the first بالحق is a fronted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in أنزلناه, and the second بالحق is a fronted ḥāl from the implied pronoun in نزل. It is also permissible for the bāʾ in the second to be attached to نزل by way of transitivity.

mekki-muskil:104-104.t: His saying {لفيفا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:106-106.t: His saying {وقرآنا فرقناه}: قرآن is accusative by an implied verb which فرقناه explains; its implied form is "and We divided a Quran — We divided it". It is also permissible for it to be conjoined to مبشرا ونذيرا, in the sense of "and the bearer of a Quran", then the muḍāf was omitted; in which case فرقناه is a naʿt (adjective) of the Quran.

mekki-muskil:107-107.t: His saying {للأذقان سجدا}: [سجدا is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {ويدع الْإِنْسَان بِالشَّرِّ دعاءه بِالْخَيرِ}: دعاءه is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). In the speech there is an omission; its implied form is "and man prays for evil [with a prayer like] his prayer for good"; then the qualified noun, which is دعاء, was omitted, then the annexed attribute was omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi took its place.

mekki-muskil:110-110.t: His saying {أيا مَا تدعوا}: أيّ is accusative by تدعوا, and مَا is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {عَلَيْك حسيبا}: accusative as a specification (bayān); it has also been said, as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying {انْظُر كَيفَ فضلنَا}: كيف is in the position of accusative by فضلنا, and انظر does not govern it, because the interrogative is not governed by what precedes it [Translator's note: the text reads "is governed by what precedes it", evidently missing the negation].
His saying {أكبر دَرَجَات}: أكبر is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), which is الآخرة, and درجات is accusative as a specification (bayān); likewise تفضيلا.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {ابْتِغَاء رَحْمَة} and {خشيَة إملاق}: both are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {ذُرِّيَّة من حملنَا}: ذرية is the second object of تتخذوا, according to the reading of whoever reads with tāʾ, and وكيلا is the first object; it is singular with a plural meaning. اتخذ takes two objects, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَاتخذ الله إِبْرَاهِيم خَلِيلًا. It is also permissible to make ذرية accusative as a vocative.
As for whoever reads يتخذوا with yāʾ, ذرية is the second object and nothing else; the vocative is far-fetched, because the yāʾ is for the absent [third person] while the vocative is for address, so they do not combine except remotely.
It has also been said that ذرية in both readings is a badal (substitute) from وكيل; and it has also been said it is accusative on the implication of أعني ("I mean"). In speech the nominative is permissible according to the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ, as a badal from the implied pronoun in يتخذوا; this is not good in the reading with tāʾ, because the absent is not substituted for the one addressed. The genitive is permissible as a badal from بني إسرائيل.
أن in His saying ألا يتخذوا, in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ, is in the position of accusative on the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "so that they do not take (لِئَلَّا يتخذوا)". As for whoever reads with tāʾ, أن admits three aspects. The first: it has no grammatical position and is explicative (tafsīr), meaning أي, so لا is prohibitive, and the meaning of the speech has passed from report to prohibition. The second: أن is redundant, not explicative, and the speech is a report after a report on the implication of a verb of saying; its implied form is "and We said to them: do not take". The third: أن is in the position of accusative and لا is redundant, with the preposition omitted together with أن; its implied form is "and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel because of your taking a guardian besides Me", i.e. out of aversion to your taking.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {وَلَا تقربُوا الزِّنَى}: whoever shortens الزنى makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of زنى يزني زنى, and whoever lengthens it (الزناء) makes it the maṣdar of زانى يزاني زناء ومزاناة.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {وَمن قتل مَظْلُوما}: مظلوما is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {إِنَّه كَانَ منصورا}: the hāʾ refers to the next of kin (al-walī); it has also been said, to the one killed; it has also been said, to the blood; and it has also been said, to the killing. Abū ʿUbayd said it is for the killer, its meaning being that the killer, when retaliation is taken from him in this world and he is killed, is helped [thereby]; this is far-fetched in interpretation.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {مرحا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Yaʿqūb read مَرِحًا with kasra on the rāʾ, so its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {نفورا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {خلال الديار}: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).
His saying {كلا نمد هَؤُلَاءِ}: كلا is made accusative by نمد, and هؤلاء is a badal (substitute) from كل, in the sense that the believer and the disbeliever are both provided for.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {وَقل لعبادي يَقُولُوا}: the disagreement about its counterpart in Sūrat Ibrāhīm has passed, and this is like it.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {أَيهمْ أقرب}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is also permissible for أيهم to mean الذي, as a badal (substitute) from the wāw in يبتغون; its implied form is "the one of them who is nearest seeks the means". On this assumption أيّ is indeclinable (mabnī) according to Sībawayh; there is disagreement and room for consideration in this, which we will mention in Sūrat Maryam, peace be upon her, if Allah the Exalted wills.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {وَمَا منعنَا أَن نرسل بِالْآيَاتِ إِلَّا أَن كذب}: the first أن is in the position of accusative as the second object of منع, and the second أن is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of منع; its implied form is "nothing prevented Us from sending the signs that Quraysh proposed except the former peoples' denial of their like", and that was the cause of their destruction; had He sent them to Quraysh and they denied them, they would have been destroyed, and it had already been decreed in Allah the Exalted's knowledge that their punishment would be deferred to the Day of Resurrection, so He did not send them for that reason.
His saying {مبصرة}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {نفيرا}: accusative as a specification (bayān).
His saying {إِمَّا يبلغن عنْدك}: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with a doubled nūn and an alif, as a dual (يبلغانّ), because the parents were mentioned before; and the pronoun was repeated in أحدهما by way of emphasis, just as He said أموات and then غير أَحيَاء by way of emphasis; so أحدهما is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun, and أو كلاهما is conjoined to أحدهما. It has also been said that the verb was made dual while it precedes [its agent], according to the dialect of those who say قاما أخواك ("your two brothers stood"), just as the sign of the feminine is retained in a preceding verb by all the Arabs; on this view أحدهما is nominative as the agent of its verb, and كلاهما is conjoined to أحدهما.

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {والشجرة الملعونة}: الشجرة is accusative by conjunction to الرؤيا, i.e. "and We did not make the vision and the accursed tree [but a trial]".

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His saying {خلقت طينا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {يَوْم ندعوا كل أنَاس بإمامهم}: the governor of يوم is a verb indicated by the speech, as though He said "they will not be wronged on the day We call", indicated by His saying وَلَا يظْلمُونَ فتيلا. It is not good for ندعو to govern it, because يوم is annexed to it [Translator's note: the text says "because يوم is a muḍāf ilayhi"], and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf, since the two are like a single noun, and a thing does not govern itself.
The bāʾ in بإمامهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ندعو, in the position of the second object of ندعو, reached by a preposition. It is also permissible for the bāʾ to be attached to an omitted [word], the omitted [word] being in the position of a ḥāl, so the implied form is "We call every people mixed with their leader", i.e. in this state; its meaning is "We call them while their leader is among them". Its meaning according to the first view is "We call them by the name of their leader", and this is the meaning of what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās in his exegesis.
It is related from al-Ḥasan that the imām here is the book in which their deeds are; on this view the bāʾ can only be attached to an omitted [word], which is in the position of a ḥāl; its implied form is "We call them while their book containing their deeds is with them", as though in the implied form it were "We call them with their book established with them" or "settled with them", and the like. On this interpretation ندعو takes only one object.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {وعد الْآخِرَة}: its meaning is "the promise of the last time", then [the noun] was omitted. So it is originally an attribute that has taken the place of the qualified noun, because الآخرة is a naʿt (adjective) of المرة; المرة was omitted and الآخرة was put in its place. The speech refers back to His saying, the Exalted, لتفسدن فِي الأَرْض مرَّتَيْنِ.
His saying {وليتبروا مَا علوا}: مَا with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and to destroy their ascendancy", i.e. the time of their ascendancy, i.e. to ruin and spoil [all] during the time of their power. It is like your saying جئْتُك مقدم الْحَاج وخفوق النَّجْم ("I came to you at the arrival of the pilgrims and the setting of the star"), i.e. at the time of that.

mekki-muskil:72-72.t:
His saying {فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَة أعمى}: it is from blindness of the heart, so it is triliteral, from عمي; therefore it came without [an auxiliary] triliteral verb, and it carries the meaning of wonder (taʿajjub). Had it been from blindness of the eye, He would have said "he will be in the Hereafter more intensely blind (أَشد عمى)" or "more evidently blind (أبين عمى)", because it carries the meaning of wonder, and blindness of the eye is a fixed thing, like the hand and the foot, so wonder at it is expressed only by means of a triliteral verb; likewise is the ruling of whatever runs in the manner of wonder.
It has also been said: since blindness of the eye is originally quadriliteral (أعمى), wonder is not expressed at it except by bringing in a triliteral verb, so that the [form of] wonder transfers it to the quadriliteral; and when the verb of the thing wondered at is quadriliteral, it cannot be transferred to more than that, so a triliteral verb must be brought in, such as بان, شدّ, كثر and the like. This is the doctrine of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ related مَا أعماه ("how blind he is!") and مَا أعوره ("how one-eyed he is!"), and the Basrans do not permit it.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t: His saying {سنة من قد}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. Allah established that as a practice, meaning Allah established that whoever expels his prophet perishes. Al-Farrāʾ said the meaning is "like the practice of those whom (كَسنة من)", and when the kāf was dropped it became accusative.

mekki-muskil:78-78.t: His saying {وَقُرْآن الْفجْر}: accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and recite the recitation of dawn"; it has also been said its implied form is "establish the recitation of dawn".

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {عَسى ربكُم أَن يَرْحَمكُمْ}: أن is in the position of accusative by عسى; the explanation of that has passed. "وال هنا" [Translator's note: so in the text, apparently corrupt; the sense seems to be "and [the mercy] here is"] the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ; and عسى from Allah is a binding certainty, and that indeed came to pass.

mekki-muskil:92-92.t: His saying {قبيلا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:94-94.t:
His saying {وَمَا منع النَّاس أَن يُؤمنُوا}: أن is in the position of accusative as the second object of منع.
His saying {إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا}: أن is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of منع, i.e. "nothing prevented people from believing except their saying such-and-such".

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {كفى بِاللَّه شَهِيدا}: Allah, exalted be His mention, is in the position of nominative by كفى, and شهيدا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a specification (bayān); its implied form is "say: Allah suffices as a witness".
